body.statement: For every covariance tuple \(\theta\) satisfying \(\Sigma_0\succ0\), \(\operatorname{rank}(Q)=r\), and \(\operatorname{range}(\Delta_e)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(Q)\) for all \(1\le e\le E\), \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{LDL}}(\theta)\).  Equivalently, a labeled size-\(r\) set is compatible if and only if some ordering has a positive-definite reference principal block whose unique unit-lower \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) factor simultaneously transforms every target-block shift to a diagonal entrywise-nonnegative matrix.
body.justification: This is the necessary-and-sufficient population kernel that replaces nonsharp target supersets by the complete labeled fiber.
body.gap: Yang, Salehkaleybar, and Kiyavash characterize a superset under latent confounding, while BACKSHIFT and coroICA identify a global mixing matrix only when variance profiles separate; none characterizes all labeled acyclic target sets at profile collisions.
body.consumer: Unknown-target perturbation studies can report all and only covariance-compatible effective target sets while retaining stationary latent confounding and measurement error.
body.proof_tex:
We prove the two inclusions without identifying the causal target with the observable certificate by definition.

First let \(T\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)\), and choose its witnessing model \(\mu\in\mathcal M_{d,E,r}\).  Set \(U=U_{\mu}\), and order all observed labels topologically so that \(U=(I_d-B_{\mu})^{-1}\) is unit lower triangular.  Let \(t\) be the induced order on the target labels and put \(A=UP_t^{\mathsf T}\), the matrix of target columns of \(U\).  Stationarity of \(H_e\) and \(\eta_e\), mutual independence of the primitive blocks, and absence of off-target shifts give, for every \(e\ge1\),
\[
 \Delta_e
 =U\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_e)U^{\mathsf T}
 =A\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_{e,t_1},\ldots,\lambda_{e,t_r})A^{\mathsf T}. \tag{8}
\]
The target principal submatrix \(P_tA=U_{tt}\) is unit lower triangular: it is a principal submatrix of \(U\) with its indices retained in topological order.  By the common-reference assumption, all reference coefficients in (8) are strictly positive.  Consequently
\[
 Q_{tt}=U_{tt}\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_{1,t_1},\ldots,\lambda_{1,t_r})U_{tt}^{\mathsf T}\succ0. \tag{9}
\]
The positive unit-lower \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) factorization is unique.  To verify the only fact used here, compare two such factorizations and their \((1,1)\) entries and first columns; these determine the first diagonal pivot and the entries below it.  Subtracting that rank-one term leaves the corresponding \((r-1)\)-dimensional factorizations, so induction determines every column and pivot.  Applying this uniqueness to (9) gives
\[
 L_t=U_{tt},\qquad
 D_t=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_{1,t_1},\ldots,\lambda_{1,t_r}). \tag{10}
\]
Taking the \(t\)-principal block of (8) and using (10),
\[
 \Lambda_{e,t}
 =L_t^{-1}P_t\Delta_eP_t^{\mathsf T}L_t^{-\mathsf T}
 =\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_{e,t_1},\ldots,\lambda_{e,t_r}), \tag{11}
\]
which is diagonal and entrywise nonnegative by \(\text{ass:nonnegative-variance-shifts}\).  Thus \(\operatorname{Cert}(\theta,T,t)\) holds, proving
\(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)\subseteq\mathcal F_{\mathrm{LDL}}(\theta)\).

Conversely, if \(T\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{LDL}}(\theta)\), then \(\text{def:algebraic-target-fiber}\) supplies an ordering \(t\) with \(\operatorname{Cert}(\theta,T,t)\).  The hypotheses of \(\text{thm:positive-noise-realization}\) are precisely the baseline positivity, exact reference rank, and common shift range assumed here.  That theorem constructs a model \(\mu\in\mathcal M_{d,E,r}\) with \(T_{\mu}=T\) and covariance tuple \(\theta\).  Hence \(T\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)\), proving the reverse inclusion.  Combining the inclusions yields the equality of fibers.  Finally, expanding \(\text{def:algebraic-target-fiber}\) and \(\text{def:ordered-ldl-certificate}\) gives exactly the stated necessary-and-sufficient ordered principal-block recovery map.
